title: Swarm wave 2: editable input node, renderer fills/multi-line/KeySpecial, monitor composer

swarm.convention: GY-WAVE2-SWARM (concurrent agents, exclusive crate ownership, frozen interface contract, central integration gate)

assignments.J1: goya-ir + goya-lang: Node::Input{placeholder}, @input scene syntax, SceneCell/DrawNode is_input, hit_test matches inputs, 4 new tests
assignments.J2: goya-wayland: present/present_dirty fills:&[Option<u32>] slice, multi-line text raster (glyph_px*1.4, rect-clipped), PlatformEvent::KeySpecial(KeySpecial) evdev arrows/home/end/delete/escape/tab, new fill/multiline/key tests
assignments.J3: goya-zcode: pure Composer state machine (char-offset cursor, UTF-8 safe, history cap 16, drafts), @input composer in scene, live focus/typing wiring, headless composer acceptance

gate_record.goya_hello_migration: workspace build green post-wave; all four bins compile against the new present/present_dirty signatures

verification.zcode_monitor_stdin_dump_live: link Connecting->Up, session list loaded, subscribed to live session
verification.zcode_monitor_live_wayland: window presented, 358 frames over 6s acceptance run

keyboard_layout_follow_up.implementation: goya-wayland consumes compositor XKB_V1 keymaps up to 16 MiB, updates client state from Wayland modifier/layout masks, translates evdev keycodes (+8) to Unicode, and preserves Enter/Backspace events. Unsupported maps use the bounded US fallback; dead-key composition is not implemented.
keyboard_layout_follow_up.live_keyboard_acceptance: not established; unit keymap tests do not demonstrate physical/compositor input delivery

notes: Monitor stays read-only: Enter echoes composed line as '[local] ...'; sending requires session/send + v4 admission (later increment).
Doctests excluded per known host rustdoc LLVM issue (README).
kaptaind auto-committer captured and committed agent work mid-flight (incl. one temporary J1 patch later reverted); final tree verified by the gate gates above.
The initial Wave-2 keyboard implementation used a US-subset ASCII map; the keyboard_layout_follow_up records the XKB keymap implementation and its remaining live acceptance limit.
